title: Off-Cycle Performance Snapshots and Calibration Process
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines Redwood Inference’s process for running off-cycle performance snapshots and the subsequent calibration protocol. Off-cycle snapshots are lightweight, evidence-backed evaluations used when a formal quarterly or annual review is not appropriate but a documented assessment is required (e.g., role change, manager transition, accelerated promotion consideration, serious performance concern, or return-from-leave reintegration).

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time and fixed-term employees globally.
- Excludes contractors on engagements shorter than 90 days unless a manager requests evidence for a conversion decision.
- Operated by People Ops in partnership with the employee’s manager and the manager’s manager for calibration.

Why we run off-cycle snapshots:
- Provide consistent, time-bounded evidence to support ad-hoc talent decisions.
- Reduce bias by using a shared rubric and normalization step.
- Keep evidence lightweight (2–4 artifacts + calibrated rating) to avoid review fatigue.

Definitions:
- Snapshot: A 7–14 calendar day evidence collection and assessment for an individual.
- Snapshot Outcome: One of {No Action, Focus Plan (30–60d), Promotion Recommendation, Role Alignment Review, Offboarding Recommendation}.
- Calibration Review: A decision meeting where managers compare snapshots and normalize ratings before People Ops finalizes outcomes.

Triggers (non-exhaustive):
1) Promotion acceleration request (manager-submitted).
2) Manager change or reassignment.
3) Return from leave >60 days seeking role/level confirmation.
4) Clear performance regression observed and requiring documented short-term intervention.
5) Role misalignment identified during onboarding or cross-functional transfer.

Process (step-by-step):
1) Initiation (Day 0)
   - Owner: Manager or People Ops.
   - Action: Complete the Snapshot Intake Form (see Appendix A). Form fields include trigger type, proposed outcome, core evidence items, and deadline (7–14 days).
   - SLA: People Ops acknowledges request within 1 business day.
2) Evidence Collection (Days 1–10)
   - Owner: Manager + Employee.
   - Required artifacts (pick at least 2):
     • Recent code PRs or design docs with reviewer comments (if applicable).
     • Customer/partner feedback emails or support tickets.
     • Product metrics/experiments showing impact (dashboard links).
     • Peer feedback (2–3 short notes; use standardized feedback template).
     • On-call incident participation notes or post-incident analysis.
   - Optional artifacts: training completion certificates, mentor notes, speed-of-delivery metrics.
3) Manager Assessment (within 2 business days of evidence close)
   - Owner: Manager.
   - Action: Complete the Snapshot Assessment using the standardized rubric (Skills, Impact, Autonomy, Collaboration). Each dimension scored on a 1–5 scale with 1–2 = Below Expectations, 3 = Meets Expectations, 4 = Exceeds, 5 = Strongly Exceeds.
   - Deliverable: One-page assessment summary and suggested Snapshot Outcome.
4) Peer/Counterbalance Review (optional for high-impact or promotion requests)
   - Owner: Cross-functional peer reviewers (identified by manager).
   - Action: Provide short corroborating comments (use People Ops micro-feedback form).
5) Calibration Review (within 7 business days of manager assessment)
   - Owner: People Ops facilitates.
   - Participants: Manager, Manager’s Manager, People Ops representative; for promotions, include a Leveling Panel member from Product or Eng leadership.
   - Agenda: Pre-read distribution, 10–15 minute discussion per snapshot, normalization, and final outcome recording.
   - Decision authority: Manager’s Manager signs off on outcome; People Ops records the decision and next steps.
6) Outcome communication (within 2 business days of calibration)
   - Owner: Manager (with People Ops copy).
   - Action: Deliver outcome to employee in one-on-one; for Focus Plans or Promotion Recommendations, attach a written plan or promotion packet template.
7) Follow-up and Closure
   - Owner: Manager and People Ops.
   - Action: Track Focus Plan progress weekly; for Promotions, assemble full promotion packet within 30 days and follow standard promotion workflow.

Timelines and SLAs:
- Acknowledgement: 1 business day after initiation.
- Evidence window: 7–14 calendar days (default 10).
- Calibration completion: within 7 business days of manager assessment.
- Outcome communicated: within 2 business days of calibration.
- Total end-to-end target: 21 calendar days.

Standardized Rubric (short):
- Skills (technical / role skills): 1–5
- Impact (customer, revenue, product): 1–5
- Autonomy (problem solving, decision quality): 1–5
- Collaboration (communication, cross-team work, mentorship): 1–5
- Notes: Attach concrete evidence links and one-line summary per dimension.

Normalization guidance:
- Use historical distribution: mean rating per level documented in Leveling Panel page.
- If manager’s suggested outcome differs from distribution by >1 level, Manager’s Manager must present concrete evidence during calibration.
- For promotions, require at least two independent corroborating artifacts beyond manager testimony.

Decision matrix (example):
- Average score <2.5 -> Focus Plan or Offboarding Recommendation (depending on evidence severity).
- Average score 2.5–3.5 -> No Action or Development Focus Plan.
- Average score 3.6–4.2 -> Meets to Exceeds: consider stretch assignments or role alignment.
- Average score >4.2 -> Promotion Recommendation (requires corroboration).

Table: Snapshot outcomes and owner actions

| Outcome | Required artifacts | Next owner action | Timebox |
|---------|--------------------|-------------------|---------|
| No Action | Assessment summary | Document in HRIS; monitor via normal cadence | 0–30 days |
| Focus Plan | Assessment + 2 evidence links | 30–60d plan, weekly check-ins, people-ops notified | 30–60 days |
| Promotion Recommendation | Assessment + 3 artifacts + peer notes | Assemble promotion packet, Leveling Panel | 30 days |
| Role Alignment Review | Role description + gap analysis | Manager & Hiring Partner to propose options | 14–30 days |
| Offboarding Recommendation | Incident logs + formal warnings | Escalate to People Ops + Legal for next steps | immediate |

Manager responsibilities checklist:
- Initiate Snapshot Intake Form for eligible triggers.
- Collect at least two artifacts and request peer feedback where required.
- Complete rubric with clear evidence links and one-paragraph narrative.
- Attend calibration and present the case concisely.
- Deliver outcome and follow-up plan to the employee.

People Ops responsibilities:
- Validate that paperwork and privacy-sensitive items are redacted.
- Schedule calibration meetings and distribute pre-reads.
- Record outcomes in HRIS and maintain snapshot audit trail.
- Monitor metrics and publish quarterly summary of off-cycle snapshot outcomes by team (anonymized).

Appeals and Escalations:
- Employees may request clarification within 5 business days of outcome.
- If the employee disputes a Promotion Recommendation denial, they can request an appeal to the Leveling Panel within 10 business days.
- Managers may escalate timeliness concerns to the People Ops Director.

Privacy and evidence handling:
- All snapshot documentation is confidential and stored in the HRIS restricted folder with role-based access.
- Sensitive customer data must be redacted unless the employee has explicit permission to share.

Measurement and KPIs (sample):
- Time to outcome (target 21 days).
- Percentage of snapshots that lead to promotion recommendations.
- Distribution variance vs. quarterly reviews (target < 10% variance).
- Employee satisfaction with process (pulse survey after closure).

Appendix A — Snapshot Intake Form (example YAML snippet):

---
trigger: "manager_promotion_request"
proposed_outcome: "promotion_recommendation"
requested_deadline: "2026-02-17"
artifacts:
  - "PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1234"
  - "Customer email: redacted@example.com"
peer_reviewers:
  - "eng-peer@example.com"
notes: "Employee led the new request routing feature and achieved 18% latency improvement."
---

Appendix B — Suggested manager communication templates (short):
- Promotion approval: "Congratulations — after calibration we are recommending promotion to [level]. Next steps: People Ops will assemble the packet and confirm comp. We will meet on [date] to discuss details."
- Focus Plan start: "We are starting a 45-day development plan focused on [skill]. We will meet weekly to review progress. I will document expectations and success criteria."
- No Action: "After review, we are not changing your level/comp at this time. We acknowledge recent work and will continue monitoring as part of regular check-ins."

Governance and review cadence:
- People Ops will review the off-cycle snapshot process annually and update rubrics based on observed variance and stakeholder feedback.
- Quarterly anonymized summary reports will be shared with People Ops leadership and Engineering HR partners.
